newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Many Tamil women die in attacks on Sri Lanka army.
newsitem.headline: Many Tamil women die in attacks on Sri Lanka army.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces killed more than 450 Tamil Tiger rebels, many of them women, staging counter-attacks on army advances towards the northern guerrilla stronghold of Kilinochchi, a military spokesman said on Friday.

He said 75 government soldiers, including five officers, were also killed in the fighting on Thursday, the fiercest since troops launched a fresh offensive towards the town on Sunday after a lull of more than a month.

The spokesman said more than 1,000 members of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) had launched two simultaneous counter-attacks from the west and the south of an army column advancing on Kilinochchi.
"Troops fought back valiantly, completely repulsing the attack, although the terrorists used human wave tactics," he said. The soldiers struck the rebels with artillery and mortars.
He said some guerrillas had managed to penetrate the western defences before they were completely overpowered. Suicide bombers set off blasts near the troops who fired on them.

"Ground troops confirmed over 450 terrorists were killed at both locations of the counter-attacks and over 300 wounded," he said. "Seventy-five army personnel including five officers were killed. Ten officers and 146 soldiers were wounded."
The spokesman said troops had recovered 138 bodies of rebel terrorists. Most of the bodies were women.
"The security forces today contacted the ICRC (International Committee of the Red Cross) in order to hand over the dead bodies of the large number of LTTE cadres," he said.
Gerard Peytrignet, ICRC representative in Sri Lanka, confirmed receiving the offer but said:
"We informed the military the ICRC could not deliver the bodies to the LTTE because we could not work out practical or logistical demands in the warring area."

Thursday's deaths bring the toll for LTTE dead and wounded to more than 1,000 in five days of the renewed war, according to the military. It puts the army's death toll at 146 and the number of wounded at just over 300.
A military officer told Reuters on Thursday at least 100 Sri Lankan soldiers were killed in a rebel pre-dawn raid but the spokesman said only 75 had been confirmed dead.
The LTTE has said only scores of its cadres were killed.
It was not possible to verify conflicting claims of the warring parties as the government has banned journalists from the war zone.
The ministry spokesman said the army could not advance further towards Kilinochchi after Thursday's fighting.

The LTTE, fighting a 13-year war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, said in their daily radio broadcast on Thursday that they were engaging the troops with "increased fierceness".
A senior British politician said on Friday his government was willing to mediate a settlement between the Sri Lankan government and separatist Tamils.

Liam Fox, under-secretary of state at the British Foreign and Commonwealth Office, told a news conference in Colombo that London could play a third-party role to end the ethnic war if invited by Colombo and rebels.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the conflict since it began in 1983.
The armed forces have targeted Kilinochchi since the Tigers overran the military's northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of more than 1,000 men.
